key_insight: Distal weight-bearing implant performance depends on coupling load-bearing geometry with durable, bone-integrating biomaterial interfaces.
engineering_relevance: Implant design must balance gait-dependent stresses and micromotion with coating integrity, fatigue resistance, and biological fixation.
method: Systematic review of implant geometry, biomaterials, and clinical translation.
Synthesis of gait-phase finite element modeling and graded Ti–hydroxyapatite interfaces.
Quantitative trend analysis of evidence maturity and validation depth.
evidence_signal: The review analyzed 34 direct-contribution papers and 32 empirical studies; more than half of the empirical evidence remained at bench or simulation level.
watch_item: Graded Ti–hydroxyapatite architectures are supported mainly by non-DWBI analog studies, so DWBI-specific durability and clinical benefit remain unvalidated.
paper_title: Biomaterials and biomechanical design of distal weight-bearing implants: Computational modeling, biomaterial interfaces, and clinical translation
